Pull back and reveal
Tell a normal story. Everything sounds fine. Then add one fact at the end that changes everything.
At karaoke last night, I sang my best song ever. Every note was perfect. The microphone was off.
The wrong worry
Say three big problems. Then say the tiny thing you were really worried about.
The car broke down, it started to rain, and my phone died. I was mostly worried about the ice cream.
Out of ten
Give something a score out of ten. It sounds like praise. Then show what the number really counts.
I give my holiday an eight out of ten. It rained on eight of the ten days.
The honest ad
Say it like an advert. Then add the small print: the tiny words at the bottom. Make them honest.
Gym membership: unlimited access, all year. Small print: you have to go.
Just ___ with ___
Say a fancy thing is really a plain thing, plus one small extra.
A smoothie is just a salad with a straw.
One word too many
Say a big, serious sentence. Then add one small word that almost cancels it.
I always tell the truth. Usually.
Lesson one
Say you have done something for many years. Then give your best advice. It is tiny and practical.
After years of travel, my best advice: pack socks. Lesson two: more socks.
The time jump
Say a small failure from today. Then say the same failure from years ago. Back then it was worse.
Today I burned the toast. Twenty years ago I burned the kitchen.
The apology that makes it worse
Say sorry. Then give an excuse. The excuse makes it worse.
Sorry I'm late. My excuse? I live next door.
Misplaced pride
Say you are proud of something. But it is tiny, or not really good.
I'm proud to say I have never once read the instructions.
What the word means in my body
Say what a word means. Then say what it means in your own body.
Holiday means rest. In my body, it means sunburn.
Plan versus done
List what you planned to do today. Then say what you really did. One small thing.
Today's plan: gym, emails, wash the car. Done: I wrote this list.
Advice I don't take
Say the advice you give other people. Then say you do the opposite.
I tell my friends to sleep early. I'm writing this at midnight.
They're right, and worse
Someone says something bad about you. Agree. Then make it even worse yourself.
My friend said I look tired. She's right. I just slept ten hours.
Proof that proves nothing
Say you know something is true. Then give a silly reason as the proof.
I know I'm popular. The delivery man knows my name.
The bargain
Ask for something big. Then say what you got instead. It is much smaller.
I asked the hotel for a sea view. We agreed on a painting of the sea.
The sandwich
Joke. Then one true sentence. Then a joke again.
My diet starts every Monday. Changing a habit is really hard. So far I have started it 150 times.
World's smallest brag
Say you are the best at something, but only in a tiny place.
I'm the best singer in my car.
Arguing with the clock
The alarm says one thing. You say another. Then say who won.
The alarm said six. I said five more minutes. I woke up at nine.
Take it back a little
Say something big that you really mean. Then make it a little smaller. Then smaller again.
I'd do anything for my family. Well, almost anything. Not the dishes.
